## 0. What is actually wrong — read this first

Two facts carry the whole bank, and for weeks neither was stated
anywhere plainly. The register listed OPEN WORK and the findings log
recorded every twist of the debugging, so the surface grew by one entry
per discovery while never once giving the position. **Reporting the
process is not reporting the position.**

| | items | what is true |
|---|---|---|
| **Choose a Response (cr-v1 — archived 2026-08-18)** | 0 | **Known broken.** Solvable without the audio, on two independent instruments. |
| Everything else | 7,183 | **Not known to be broken** — never read by a person |

0.0% is a quality problem. The rest is a scheduling
problem, and it is blocked on one 20-minute task: **B2 — the two never-read cohorts (B4 passed 2026-08-15)**.

Every cohort a human has actually read came back clean. The one that failed a human check — Choose a Response cr-v1 — was archived on 2026-08-18 and replaced by cr-v7.

### Every attempt to fix Choose a Response (cr-v1 — archived 2026-08-18)

`blind` is how often three AI solvers pick the right answer with the
audio withheld. `control` is the best a fixed-letter guesser could do.
**A gap near zero is the goal.** Nothing has reached it.

| attempt | changed | blind | control | gap | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **cr-v1 — original authoring** | The batch as first written. | 76.9% | — | *not recorded* | FAILED |
| **narrow repair** | Rewrote only the 24 options with the clearest defect, rather than rebuilding. | 74.4% | 29.2% | **+45.2** | REFUTED |
| **cr-v3** | New method: distractors written as the correct reply to a near-miss version of the spoken line. | 77.8% | 25% | **+52.8** | FAILED |
| **cr-v4** | Varied the spoken line: good news, a request, an offer, a correction, an apology, an announcement. | 47.2% | 25% | **+22.2** | INCONCLUSIVE |
| **cr-v5** | cr-v4 plus a ban on one give-away phrase the solvers named. | 72.2% | 25% | **+47.2** | FAILED |
| **cr-v6** | cr-v4's brief held EXACTLY — nothing added, nothing removed, fresh scenarios. The replication test. | 72.2% | 25% | **+47.2** | FAILED |
| **cr-v7** | New METHOD, not a new brief: four mutually exclusive worlds per item authored symmetrically (each world has its own line AND reply; 1,584 kill-quotes machine-verified), then a seeded RNG picks the spoken world AFTER the text is frozen — no author ever knows the key. | 26.4% | 25% | **+1.4** | CLEARED |

The shape of that table is the finding: **each attempt removes the
previous tell and introduces a new one.** Why each failed:

- **cr-v1 — original authoring** — The brief fixed four kinds of wrong answer — over-formal, rude, dismissive, topic-shifting. The key is then simply the option that is none of them, and all three solvers named the roster unprompted.
- **narrow repair** — Removing one of four slots leaves three, and the key is still the option that is none of them. Moved the score ~3 points; I predicted 28.4% beforehand and was wrong by 46.
- **cr-v3** — The method was sound but every spoken line was the same kind of line — two-part bad news — so the key was always rueful acceptance and the distractors always relief or disbelief. The roster moved from the answers up to the questions and got stronger.
- **cr-v4** — BEST RESULT. Solvers stayed confident, used the same heuristic, and got worse — the signature of a tell actually removed. Inside the pre-registered 20-30 band at n=12, so not a pass, and never re-tested unchanged.
- **cr-v5** — The ban stripped questions out of the wrong answers, so pre-flight flagged an imbalance, and repairing THAT by hand made every wrong answer sound hedgy — "I thought", "I gather" — in 6 of 36 distractors and 0 of 12 keys. I reintroduced a roster while fixing a cosmetic check.
- **cr-v6** — +47.2, indistinguishable from cr-v5 and from the original defect: cr-v4's +22.2 was a draw, not a method. This settled that no BRIEF fixes the task type — the authorship asymmetry (the key is the reply to the real line, the distractors are something else) survives every authoring rule.
- **cr-v7** — CLEARED AND SHIPPED 2026-08-18 on Andy's explicit approval. The key is statistically independent of every text feature by construction; the solvers' loudest heuristic was counted against the population and points nowhere (15.8% where chance is 25%). S1 −16.7, S2 +1.4, post-cohesion re-attack +5.6, all under the pre-registered +30 kill bar. 132 items live as cohort cr-v7; the 63 old rows archived; the Listening blueprint restored to the ETS shape (14 delivered).

## 1. Where every cohort actually stands — MEASURED

`blind` is 3 AI solvers with the source withheld, against a 25%
control. `human` is a real reviewer under the same protocol. **Where
the two disagree the human wins** — the finding of 2026-08-06, and on
Announcement and Daily Life the model was indeed the one that was wrong.

Two qualifications, both learned the hard way:

- `human` is the **best single reader**, never a pooled average. The
  question is whether a person *can* shortcut these items, and one
  reader who can settles it. Pooling a diligent reader with a cautious
  one produced "cleared by hand" for a cohort scoring 74.4% blind.
- The human winning does not mean the model was noise. Where a reader
  also clears the control by a wide margin, the two AGREE and the cohort
  is confirmed broken — which is what happened to Choose a Response.

### Excluded from the human column — model-assisted

34 reviews were entered through the human UI with a model
doing the answering. They are kept as data and marked `model_assisted`
(migration 079); they do NOT feed the `human` column above, because that
column is worth exactly one thing — being the number a model did not
produce.

- `academic-passage-2026-08-06` — 13/20 (65.0%)
- `craft-and-structure-2026-08-06` — 14/14 (100.0%)

**79.4% assisted vs 19.7% by hand.** That gap is
the point: a model reading four options scores far above a person doing
the same, which is exactly why one of the two instruments has to stay
human. Unfiltered, SAT Craft and Structure read *CONFIRMED BROKEN — both
instruments agree* on blind 97.4% + "human" 100%, condemning 211 items on
a model agreeing with itself.

## 4. Settled — do not redo

- **SAT Math derivational hub.** Claimed "bank-wide, 64.4%". It was 131 items of 820. All repaired; both cohorts now score BELOW chance. → `scripts/study-bank/MATH-HUB-RESULT.md`
- **The cheap elimination gate cannot replace the blind attack.** Fires on 3 of 32 items in a repaired batch. Once distractors are well-formed it stops correlating with anything. → `scripts/study-bank/CRV3-RESULT.md`
- **The option-balance check does not work.** Predicted a 2.7pt spread across three batches whose real margins spanned +14.6 to +40.4, and its inputs were not reproducible between labellers. → `scripts/study-bank/OPTION-BALANCE-RESULT.md`
- **Figures do not leak their answers.** 0 leaks across 164 graphics, with a 7-fixture self-test proving the checker fires on real ones and stays quiet on well-formed charts. → `scripts/study-bank/check-graphic-leak.mjs`
- **Reviews are bound to the content they judged.** Migration 076 applied. Scoring reads study_item_reviews_fresh, so editing a reviewed item visibly invalidates its review instead of silently keeping it. → `database/migrations/076_review_content_binding.sql`
- **The 120 held items are held on DIFFERENT evidence from `v2`, and the `v2` result does not release them.** `v2` ran high *including its own live control*, so 82.8% was the instrument's level on that material and never a deviation. The held reading batches deviate from a matched control that sits **at chance**: shipped ssat/reading measures 21.1% against a 20.0% line, while `ssat-reading-s11` came in at 66.7%, and `isee-reading-s10` at 69.4%/72.2% with the cross-item channel designed out by construction. A deviation from a floor-at-chance control is a stronger claim than a high absolute number. Decided 2026-09-12: do **not** release `ssat-reading-s11`, `ssat-reading-s12`, `isee-reading-s10` or `sat-cs-h4` on the strength of the `v2` finding. The open question is narrower and is not settled — nobody has tested whether a model *deviation* transfers to a human, only that model *levels* do not. → `scripts/study-bank/REGISTER.md section 5 (2026-09-12, the v2 finding)`
- **A model options-only number on a PROSE cohort may not be cited to repair or archive live items.** Established 2026-09-12 on `v2` (see §5). It stays a verdict on numeric maths, where the option set is bare values carrying no recall prior. Consequence: the SSAT Verbal (180 items) and ACT English recommendations are **not executable** until a human sits a sample — and per the width finding in §5, that sitting was not even drawable until today. → `scripts/study-bank/REGISTER.md section 5 (2026-09-12, the v2 finding)`
- **Author maths, do not author reading.** Maths is where the attack is a verdict rather than a screen, and 258 items cleared it in one day. Reading has failed six consecutive rewrites; the unit of repair is the **passage set**, not the item, and no brief has yet addressed that. Do not commission a seventh reading rewrite to the same shape. → `scripts/study-bank/READING-PILOT-KILLED.md`
- **Key extremity is diffuse, not a cohort: no repair programme, gated at authoring.** Live SAT keys sit at an extreme 31.1% vs a 50% derived line (ACT 43.1%, SSAT 20.0% vs 40, ISEE 41.9%), spread across every cohort; repairing all of v2 would cut the SAT exploit only from +9.1 to ~+6.0 pts. No item rewrite. Instead key-extremity-gate.mjs refuses a maths batch under 0.8 x derived chance at insert (2026-10-02). → `scripts/study-bank/KEY-EXTREMITY-RESULT.md`
- **The grader is not calibrated, and cannot be from public data.** Only two scored ETS samples exist for our task types. Do not tune prompts against them — two items cannot support fitting.

- **2026-09-21** — **"STUDENTS ARE RUNNING OUT OF SSAT TESTS": THEY WERE GETTING ONE CLEAN TEST, NOT THREE, AND NOTHING ANYWHERE FAILED.** A student's first four SSAT reading sections delivered **40/40 fresh, 36/40, 2/40, 0/40** — the third test was 95% questions they had already answered. The bank was not the constraint: 138 reading items sit in 31 passages (13 of six, 7 of five, 11 smaller) and the draw could only ever reach the thirteen. `drawByPassage` regrouped rows the caller had ranked unseen-first and then sorted the GROUPS by "full first, largest first" — **size is a property of the bank and does not change between sittings, so the same thirteen passages won every draw for ever**, stranding 56 items (41% of the reading bank) permanently. The section was always 40 questions and always on time, because the function tops up from whatever remains; the failure mode is silent by construction. **Fix:** `drawByPassage` takes an optional freshness predicate and ranks passages by how many UNSEEN items they can supply (capped at `perPassage`), then by fullness, then size — with no predicate the expression collapses to the old ordering exactly, so the previous behaviour is the special case rather than a branch. Counting fresh items rather than asking "any fresh?" is load-bearing: it is what separates an untouched five-question passage from a six-question one with a single item left, and it moved form 2 from 36/40 to 40/40. **Measured against the real draw: SSAT reading 1 → 3 clean forms, ISEE reading 1 → 2, SSAT overall 1 → 2 complete repeat-free tests** (the binding section is now Verbal, whose 180 items sit in 136 bijective groups — a bank-depth problem, not a draw bug). Break-tested both ways: reverting the ranking returns form 2 to 30/40 and caps lifetime reach at exactly the 78 stranded items; removing the call-site predicate fails the wiring guard. **`form-capacity.mjs` was reporting SSAT as 4/3/3 and labelling each line "this number is exact"** — the division is exact, the claim that items/form-size is capacity is not, and it was wrong in the flattering direction; that label now reads UPPER BOUND and points at the new `admission-form-depth.ts`, which replays the real assembler. Two lessons: **a uniform test fixture cannot see a defect that only appears when group sizes vary** (982 passing tests, all using equal-sized passages, never touched this), and **`takePassages` — the ACT path, in the same file — iterates groups in the caller's ranked order and has never had this bug**, so one file held both the right and the wrong way to do it. **Confirmed against live exposures, not only simulation:** of the two students with SSAT history, the one who has sat it in volume has seen **exactly 78 distinct reading items** — 13 x 6, the stranded ceiling to the item, against 160 of 180 verbal and 100 of 214 math. The bank held 138 reading items and 60 of them had never been served to anyone. → **A31**

THE SHUFFLE IS CURRENTLY HIDING OUR OWN AUTHORING SKEW.** A grader raised it as a format nit — *"numeric choices are in scrambled order; a real ACT orders them monotonically"* — and it opens onto something structural.

  **Measured.** Authored order in the bank is already only partly monotonic (sat/math **27.1%**, act/math **42.3%**, isee **76.2%**, ssat **61.0%**, against 8.3% by chance for four distinct values).   **THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG, AND THE NUMBER FROM THE ENTRY ABOVE IS WHY.** Sorting numeric options for fidelity converts MAGNITUDE rank into LETTER position, and this bank's keys are not flat by magnitude:

        cohort               key is a middle rank    sorted, "always pick B or C" scores
        sat/math v2          578/790 = 73.2%         36.6%   (+11.6 over chance)
        sat/math others      177/297 = 59.6%         29.8%   (+4.8)
        isee/math            187/319 = 58.6%         29.3%   (+4.3)
        act/math             234/423 = 55.3%         27.7%   (+2.7)

  So sorting would hand a student a **positional** tell worth up to +11.6 points, requiring no magnitude comparison at all — just "pick B or C". **The shuffle is not preventing a defect; it is concealing one.** That is a worse state than either alternative, because the concealment is invisible and the defect keeps being authored.

  **THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS THE FINDING.** Fix the magnitude distribution first — bring key-is-middle toward what a real form does — and only then sort for fidelity. Doing it the other way round publishes the skew. Doing neither leaves every maths item non-exam-shaped while the skew accumulates unmeasured. **Not taken here:** this touches live draw behaviour on ~2,000 items and depends on a number I cannot get (what the real SAT's magnitude distribution actually is), so it belongs with the `v2` decision rather than in front of it. Same shape as the NO CHANGE pin fixed this morning — an option-order convention the real exam has and we do not — but the opposite conclusion, because there the pin had no interaction and here it has a large one.

(2) `AM12I-02` and `AM12S-04` are the same question — substitute a value into a supplied linear rule — sitting in **different domains**, which is exactly why a per-domain review cleared them.         family / cohort        key is a MIDDLE rank (2 or 3 of 4 by magnitude)

This one points at the key by direct measurement over 790 items, and it needs no model, no null and no attack — a distractor set that brackets the key above and below IS the shape, and bracketing is the most natural way to write distractors, which is exactly why it is easy to do to excess.

Genuine exams do bracket, so some concentration is fidelity rather than defect, and 50% is the wrong target — a bank at exactly 50% would look unlike a real form. What is measurable is the SPREAD between our cohorts: the hand-authored ones sit at 40.9-63.2% while `v2` sits at 73.2%, so `v2` is out of line **with our own newer work**, which is a comparison that needs no external reference.

The lesson from that is exactly on point here: a measured margin against a model instrument is not a student-reachable leak. **But this one is different in kind and should be said plainly — it is arithmetic, not semantics, a student can be taught it in one sentence, and prep books do.** That is an argument for measuring it against a human, not for acting now. **Recommended: add "eliminate both extremes" to the next human sitting as an explicit instruction to one reader**, which converts it from a bank statistic into the only kind of evidence this project accepts. _(no change made; recorded with its counts, its p and its limits)_ → **B6**

- **2026-09-12** — **THE TWIN PAIR IS REAL, AND IT POINTS THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM WHAT ITS DISCOVERERS ASSUMED. EIGHTH PROXY REFUTED.** Two options-only solvers found it independently on different files, neither able to see the other, and both drew the same conclusion: *"A and D are the same clause differing only in `had put` / `put`, so neither can be uniquely correct, and the pair itself eliminates half the set."* The reasoning is clean and the mechanism is the first in a long time that is MECHANICALLY decidable rather than semantic, so it earned a checker — `check-twin-options.mjs`, which finds a pair of options far closer to each other than to the rest of the set and asks one question of it: **when a twin pair exists, is the key inside it or outside it?**

        section                 key INSIDE the twin pair
        act/english               13/17 =  76.5%
        sat/reading_writing       17/19 =  89.5%
        sat/math                   7/7  = 100.0%
        toefl/reading              5/6  =  83.3%
        ssat/reading               2/2  = 100.0%
        act/math                   0/1  =   0.0%
        POOLED                    44/52 =  84.6%   against a 50.0% chance line
                                  P(>= 44 of 52) = 2.0e-07

  **The key is inside the pair 84.6% of the time. "Eliminate the twins" would make a solver WORSE, not better** — it discards the key five times in six. The explanation is obvious once the number exists and was invisible before it: **the twin pair IS the contrast under test.** An item's key and its nearest miss are, by construction, the two most similar options in the set. The solvers' premise — *neither can be uniquely correct* — is exactly backwards: one of them is, and the pair exists precisely because the item tests that distinction. Joins run-middle, key-is-sum, key-magnitude, stem-echo, option-balance, plurality-key and the ratio hub on the dissolved list. **Eighth structural proxy built and refuted; CLAUDE.md's "every structural proxy has been too coarse" now has eight members and not one has survived contact with its own population.**

(1) It fired on `its / it is / its' / their` — **a short option set is a minimal-pair lattice BY DESIGN**, the contrast IS the item, and trigram similarity is degenerate at three characters. Guarded by a minimum length. (2) The length guard then broke the real case, because **`No Change` is nine characters**. It is now excluded from the comparison entirely — it is an opaque token carrying no orthography, so it can be neither half of a pair, which is the rule both ACT English repair agents derived independently and the one their whole method rests on.

The checker reported `NOT MEASURED` on all six and I nearly read six empty lines as six clean sections. It refused correctly; the loop was wrong. _(the only reason that was caught is that the checker prints its denominator before its verdict)_ → **A21**

        Conventions of Standard English   40/54 = 74.1%   17/25 = 68.0%     0.598
        Production of Writing             22/30 = 73.3%   14/21 = 66.7%     0.757

        by batch: v5r2 39/50 = 78.0%   v6r2 37/50 = 74.0%

LIVE EXPOSURE MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE POPULATION, not sampled: 1,719 drawable maths items (paged and ordered — the unpaged read returns 1,000 and silently omitted one of the three), 311 with at least one non-numeric option, **3 where a distractor collides with the key** — one SAT Algebra `t <= 8`/`t >= 8` (math-v3), one ISEE `x < -5`/`x > -5` (isee-math-s5), one SAT compound inequality `-12 < x <= 20`/`-12 <= x < 20` (v2). WHY IT FAILED, and this is the part worth keeping: the near-miss method worked exactly as designed. For each item I wrote one spoken line, then three near-miss lines with one fact changed, and took the natural reply to each. But every line I wrote was the SAME KIND of line — two-part mildly bad news, a constraint plus a complication. Given that stimulus, "one fact changed" almost always means the constraint is looser or absent, so near-miss replies are systematically RELIEF or DISBELIEF and the real reply is systematically RUEFUL ACCEPTANCE. All three solvers described that structure independently and unprompted; solver 1 reduced it to "pick the most inconvenient specific consequence with a follow-up question", solver 3 to "discard the relieved one, discard the '…at all?' one, discard the odd-topic one, take what remains." cr-v1 fixed a roster of distractor TYPES; cr-v3 removed it and silently installed a roster of STIMULUS types instead. The tell moved up one level and got STRONGER. That is the CLAUDE.md corollary landing for the fourth time — I wrote "vary the load-bearing element" into the brief for the distractors and then violated it one layer up, because it never occurred to me that the spoken line was a variable. REVISION 2 MUST CHANGE THE STIMULUS, NOT THE DISTRACTOR METHOD: the line must sometimes be good news, neutral, a question, a request or an offer, so that "accepts a constraint" stops being a winning guess — the key should be the relieved reply about as often as the rueful one. Under the pre-registration this is revision 1 of a maximum 2; a second failure triggers §6, reducing Choose a Response in the Listening blueprint. The brief produced its mirror. This is the CLAUDE.md corollary observed live three times in one day, and the decision recorded in ACT-ATTACK-RESULT.md is to stop: no third brief. The next instrument is a human sitting, because the register already holds seven cohorts where the AI attack said 83-100% and a person scored 13-27%. Two tooling facts worth keeping: the loop keys attack freshness on item content, so a repaired item re-enters prepare automatically and an untouched one keeps its result; and act-bank-helper update rewrites prompt/choices/key by localId within a cohort and refuses passage changes, so the batch file remains the source of truth after a repair. → **A21**

- **2026-09-12** — **THE 120 LIVE ACT SCIENCE ITEMS WERE ATTACKED FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND THE RUN DISQUALIFIED ITS OWN VERDICT.** Figure-blind render (stem + four options; passage, figure and caption withheld), leakage-free split at one item per passage group per file, keys dealt flat, 36 solvers over 12 files, pre-registered in `ACT-SCIENCE-ATTACK-PREREG-2026-09-12.md` (`29066425`) before anything ran. **ACT Science 250/360 = 69.4% (120 items, flat-deal floor 28.3%); matched live control ACT Reading — what students can already open — 168/216 = 77.8% (72 items, floor 25.0%); Δ = −8.3, inside the PASS band.** It is NOT a pass: pre-registered clause 1 fired — 12 of 36 same-file solver pairs returned byte-identical pick-strings (11 of 18 on the CONTROL, 1 of 18 on the batch), so no verdict on the hidden flag is available from this run. The clause is the wrong instrument for this design, and that is the lesson to carry: three solvers are three samples of ONE model, and on a 12-item file near-determinism produces identical strings with no collusion (mean pairwise agreement 94.4% control, 86.9% batch). The next pre-registration needs solver diversity or longer files, not a softer clause. **Clause 2 did not fire** — the control cleared its floor by 52.8 points, so the low numbers inside the batch are measurements, not a flat instrument. **THREE THINGS THE RUN DID ESTABLISH.** (1) **The 2026-08-05 maths figure-decoration defect is absent.** Figure-bearing items 67.5% vs figure-less 74.1% — lower, as predicted; `svg` charts are the LOWEST type at 61.9%, nothing like the 100% `rawsvg` geometry collapse; and an exact whole-population check (values vs labels, not sampled) found **0 of 84 items whose stem prints a measured value from its own figure** — the 6 flagged are condition labels like "the 40 °C trial" colliding with a cell elsewhere. (2) **The bank is two different tests.** Interpretation of Data 47.8% (66/138) and 20 of the 29 items no solver could touch; Evaluation of Models 86.8% (112/129) with a **confident subset of 84 of 84 = 100.0%**. The solvers' stated bases on the solved ones are background science ("autoclaving sterilizes, so it is the no-living-microbes control") and internal option consistency, not the distractor-family tells that decided English and R&W — closer to the ACT Knowledge-of-Language "nothing withheld" reading than to a leak. Rate RISES with authored difficulty (easy 64.6 / medium 68.5 / hard 75.8), which is the wrong direction. (3) **The confident-subset collapse did not happen** (batch 94.0%, control 96.0%), so the signal is real; the scorer was break-tested three ways first — constant-letter solver scores EXACTLY the printed flat floor, oracle scores 100%, one deleted answer exits non-zero rather than shrinking the denominator. **NOTHING WAS CHANGED, ARCHIVED OR INSERTED.** The hidden flag stays where it is: per the standing rule, and per `bank-act-science`'s own requirement, Science needs a HUMAN SITTING — the register holds seven cohorts where the attack said 83–100% and a person scored 13–27%, and ACT itself cleared at a co-founder's 10.0% against a model 76–79%. Full write-up in `ACT-SCIENCE-ATTACK-2026-09-12.md`. → **A21**

Implications for anything that scores this task: the opener is no longer evidence of skill, so a pilot/ability estimate should not credit position 1.
- **2026-10-02** — **A22 CLOSED: THE SIX CHECKERS NOW READ THE FILE THEY ARE HANDED — AND THE SWEEP FOUND SEVEN MORE, PLUS THREE DETECTORS THAT HAD BEEN BLIND TO PART OF THEIR OWN POPULATION.** Re-measured before fixing: `check-explanation-option-refs`, `check-explanation-ordinals`, `check-svg-viewbox` and `check-graphic-leak` still printed BYTE-IDENTICAL output for `sat-cs-hard-v3` and `act-math-v4gi` (graphic-leak took the path as a DOMAIN filter: "0 rows read … nothing to check", exit 0). `check-verbatim-key` and `check-vocab-ambiguity` had been made to refuse any argument on 2026-09-15 — honest, but no file mode, and no-argument still silently meant the live bank. All six now follow one contract in the new `checker-input.mjs`: `<batch.json> [...]` reads THAT file; `--live` is the only way to get the shipped bank and the header says `POPULATION: WHOLE LIVE BANK`; `--selftest` runs fixtures with no DB; no input, a missing file, bad JSON, a non-array, zero items, an unknown flag, `--live` plus a path, or **scorable 0 of M** all exit 2 — "0 defects over 0 SVGs" is no longer printable. `scorable N of M` prints before every verdict. Each has a RUN_AS_CLI guard (`isMain`); ordinals no longer runs its self-test on import, so `apply-ordinal-fix.mjs` now calls it explicitly. **Break-test** (`checker-input.breaktest.mjs`, no DB, 13 assertions × 6 checkers = 78, all pass): two real batches give different output, garbage/empty/object/scalar/missing each exit 2, no-args exit 2, and a planted-defect batch fires (exit 1) where its clean twin passes (0); verbatim-key, a diagnostic, moves 50.0% → 0.0% between the two. Live numbers re-run under `--live` match the old output line for line, except where the detector itself changed: **(1)** option-refs' regex was case-sensitive on the keyword, so sentence-initial "Choice C is correct" — the commonest phrasing — never matched; caught by its new fixture (live still 0); **(2)** svg-viewbox read only `rawsvg` and never the ACT inserter's `graphic.type 'svg'`: 86 → **137** live figures in the denominator, still 0 clipped; its `--fix` also referenced an undefined `h` and would have thrown on the first fixable item; **(3)** vocab-ambiguity never recognised ACT's `in the phrase "…"` or `paragraph 6` and never swept `act/reading` at all: 100 → **115** pointed stems, the new 15 all clean, still 4 ambiguous. **Sweep for the same pattern:** seven live-only tools read no argv, so a batch path was silently ignored — `check-chip-tells`, `check-conversations`, `check-duplicate-questions`, `check-shared-headword`, `check-unrendered-types`, `verify-admission-forms`, `form-capacity` — now refuse any argument (exit 2) and still run with none; `check-live-closure` and `verify-sat-hard-route.ts` took any string as a section name and now refuse anything but `math`/`reading_writing`. **Listed, not changed:** `verify-act-science-v6/v7` default to the batch they are named for; `render-distractor-pilot` defaults its input file (author tool); the `*-draw`/`-pop`/`-match` attack scripts are one-shot tooling, not checkers. **Two things this surfaced and did not fix:** `check-graphic-leak --live` reports **66** defects (54 `figure-number-in-caption`, 12 `answer-in-figure-text`), all apparently ACT Science "Figure 1" captions and an "Experiment 3"/"L-20" match on a numeric key — the §4 line "0 leaks across 164 graphics" predates ACT Science and is stale; and ordinals' batch mode inherits the detector's known prose false positives ("The first sentence…", "the third winter"). _(fixed: A22)_

- **2026-10-02** — **A23: THE SAT R&W ELIMINATION BAR IS NOW A MARGIN OVER A MATCHED LIVE CONTROL, AND BOTH OVERRIDDEN COHORTS PASS IT.** The bar was pre-registered in commit `822bdb13` before any read: candidate rate of items with >=1 confidently rejected DISTRACTOR minus control rate <= +20 pts; no verdict if the control exceeds 80% (ceiling), candidate n<12 or <3 samples per arm. Instrument: options-only, one reader per run, candidate and control rendered into SEPARATE files (interleaving was refuted 2026-09-15), keys dealt flat, 3 Claude samples per arm — one solver sampled three times, not three solvers, so no independence statistic is quoted. Controls: live rows from other cohorts, composition-matched at 2x. **Craft and Structure** (`rw-v8-cs-hard`, 16 live rows): candidate **0.0%** [0,0,0] vs control **57.3%** (n=32) [59.4, 56.3, 56.3] → margin **-57.3, PASS**. The control is v2 at 83.3% (n=22) and every newer cohort at 0% (n=10). **Standard English Conventions** (`rw-v8-sec-hard`, 22 live rows): **10.6%** vs **24.2%** (n=44) → margin **-13.6, PASS**; the two items cut in every sample are the noun+verb-inside-one-option shape named on 2026-09-04. No reader ever confidently rejected a key in either arm. Why the zero bar could never pass: reject-first lands on a distractor 95.5-97.9% of the time in BOTH arms, so removing one wrong option softly is a property of the format, not of a batch. **Caveat, recorded so it is not read as a clearance:** this instrument is stricter than the 2026-09-04 reader, which called 11 of the same 16 CS rows rejectable — and confidently rejected the KEY on 2 of them. The new readers aimed reject-first at the same flat denials and absolutes but would not call any certain. So `rw-v8-cs-hard`'s separate `tells` failure (the key is the single concede-then-qualify option) is untouched by this result; that is a key-shape tell and needs a human sitting, which this cohort has never had. **Recommendation, not action:** keep both cohorts live; schedule `rw-v8-cs-hard` into the next human SAT R&W sitting to decide the `tells` question; no item was archived, edited or hidden. `gate.mjs` now re-derives the SAT R&W elimination verdict from the recorded numbers and treats a zero-bar record as missing (`elimination-gate-selftest.mjs`: 11 cases; disabling the re-derivation decides 5 of them wrongly). Recorded as `revisits` on both ledger entries; `stages.elimination` left as historically recorded.

New words only: 0 content words from any of 547 SSAT verbal rows in any inflection (`ssat-verbal-s18-tools.mjs`, `roots()` over-matches on purpose), each word once per arm; disjoint stem letter ranges per author (A/C A–L, B/D M–Z); second author of each type checked against the first.
  - **Synonyms (72 frozen `6a2e6573`, sha 7f118181; kept sha ab9590b7).** Options-only: candidate 66/216 = 30.6% vs letter 20.8% (+9.7), live 44/120 = 36.7% vs 20.0% (+16.7), **E −6.9** (bar +10; live far below the 85% ceiling). Unanimous-correct 18.1% vs 22.5%; pairwise agreement 62.8% (one solver, three samples). Elimination 0/72 vs 0/40. Two graders 72/72 and 72/72 on key, 0 second defensible, 0 above band, 0 free eliminations, 0 antonym options. **Banked 35 easy / 35 medium / 2 hard** by the easier-label rule (graders 27/32/13 and 35/35/2), against 14/38/20 commissioned: the synonym bank gets easier (live was 53/139/73). Graders called the distractors "unrelated rather than near-miss", which is what made it easy.
  - **Analogies (80 frozen, sha 89e8a5f8).** Options-only: candidate 56/240 = 23.3% vs 20.0% (+3.3), live 60/120 = 50.0% vs 20.0% (+30.0), **E −26.7**; unanimity 6.3% vs 25.0%; elimination 0/80 vs 0/40. **Family gate: creator/creation 9/12 → HOLD** (next: degree 6/12, expert/field 6/12; worker/workplace and antonyms 0/12). Nothing graded or inserted; no repair (prereg). Diagnostic, recorded and NOT used to re-decide: the creator/creation option was picked 21 of 60 times it was present (instrument 26/60, worker/tool 24/60 — the samples named "worker:product is a common SSAT relation" as their no-signal default), but 9 of those 21 picks were right (42.9% vs ~20% for a pure prior), so it is neither cleanly a prior nor cleanly a tell; on 4 items × 3 correlated samples it is ~4 effective observations.
  - **Finding 1 — the family gate as written cannot separate a solver prior from a leak.** Conditioning on the 4 keyed items per family means any family a solver favours in the no-signal case inflates its own keyed rate, and with 20 families × correlated samples one of them reaching 9/12 is not rare. The fix for the next analogy batch is to pre-register the gate on PRECISION (right/picked when the family is present, vs its 20% design rate) with a minimum pick count, not on keyed-item hit rate. Not applied here: re-deciding a finished batch with a rule found afterwards is what pre-registration forbids.
  - **Finding 2 — the balanced-incidence design does what the batch-level attack can see.** 23.3% against a live arm at 50.0% is the lowest analogy margin measured (a17 was +3.1 against +31.1). The samples' only named structural signal was a "reversed twin" (two options sharing a relation in opposite order — not the key's relation, so a cross-family coincidence of direction) on ~8 of 120 items, mostly live.
  - **Finding 3 — a checker that loaded nothing printed PASS, again.** `check --also <one file>` skipped the file (loop bound) and printed PASS over 0 other-author items; author B noticed "other-author items 0". Fixed to refuse an empty `--also`; break-tested (B vs itself 216 collisions, B vs A PASS over 36). The first-author files were never affected (no `--also`).

A future analogy batch on new words only will need different families, or the "new words only" rule relaxed for distractors.
  - **Process.** One blind sample (ana B) used a seeded random generator for 98 no-signal picks; this dilutes both arms equally (the arms are interleaved) but weakens the instrument; sample C was told to judge every pick. Several agents batched their "save every N items" writes into one; work was not lost.

Jest 292/292 suites, 3,415 tests. → `ssat-verbal-s18.prereg.md`, `ssat-verbal-replay.ts`, `ssat-verbal-s18-{tools,stages}.mjs`, `ssat-verbal-s18.{design,live-words}.json`, `ssat-verbal-s18{a,b,c,d}.batch.json`, `ssat-verbal-s18-{syn,ana}.batch.json`, `-oo.*`, `ssat-verbal-s18-syn-g{1,2}.*`, `ssat-verbal-s18-syn.{qc,kept.batch}.json`; ledger `ssat-verbal-s18-syn-kept-2026-10-09` (shipped), `ssat-verbal-s18-ana-held-2026-10-09` (killed)

IT PASSED OPTIONS-ONLY AT E −39.0, THE BEST ANALOGY MARGIN YET, AND THE NEW PRECISION FAMILY GATE, THEN WAS HELD AT THE NEW WITH-SOURCE DIFFICULTY GATE: BANKED EASY 22/48 = 45.8% OF THE KEPT ITEMS (BAR ≤ 40%).** Analogies still bind alone: form 10 needs +30, form 11 +60. It holds at lift ≥ 10 points, p ≤ 0.05/F and picks ≥ 6. It was break-tested on s18's files before the prereg was committed. s18 as measured: PASS (creator/creation 9/21, p 0.0052 vs 0.0025). ## 6. The rule that keeps this honest

A cohort is **not** clean because the cheap checks passed. Five
structural proxies have been built — letter spread, length rank,
punctuation asymmetry, concessive pivot, option-family balance — and
each caught the tell it was built for while missing the next one. The
blind attack is the gate, a human sitting is the confirmation, and the
structural checks are pre-flight only. See CLAUDE.md.

- **2026-09-04** — **I SENT ANDY A MESSAGE ASKING HIS CO-FOUNDER TO SIT A RUN THAT HAD BEEN FINISHED TWO DAYS EARLIER.** He sat down, was served 20 questions, and correctly reported that they "didn't seem like ACT". They were not:

      act-cofounder-2026-09-02    40/40 answered, 4 correct = 10.0%
                                 done 2026-09-02 15:33-16:14 UTC — ALREADY COMPLETE
      crv10-cofounder-2026-09-03  20/20 answered, 5 correct = 25.0%  <- what he actually did
                                 done 2026-09-04 13:45-14:00 UTC, TOEFL Listening / Choose a Response

  ACT had already cleared on that 10.0% (well under the pre-registered 40% clean bar) and is shipped in `shipped-tests.ts`. `/admin/bank-qc` did exactly the right thing: with no ACT run outstanding it served the next open one, CR v10. **The instruction was wrong, not the app.**

  **Cause, and it is the third instance of one class today.** I wrote the message from this register's open-work row **B7**, which still described the ACT sitting as pending. CLAUDE.md's first rule is *"Before stating any bank fact, run bank-state.mjs"* — I ran it only afterwards, when the co-founder's report contradicted me, and it showed the completed run immediately. The other two instances today: commissioning a reading v3 that `READING-PILOT-KILLED.md` forbade (register row stale), and writing a sizing line that mapped candidate batch names onto live cohorts by name similarity. **All three are the same failure — trusting a register row instead of the data it summarises — and this one cost a person's time, which the others did not.** B7 is now closed below.

  **The silver lining is real and should not be lost:** `crv10-cofounder` is a genuine open question and it now has an answer. **20 of 20 answered, 5 correct, exactly 25.0% — dead on chance for a four-option item.** Choose a Response v10 is clean by the blind bar. That is the cohort whose earlier versions ran 55.0% (`choose-a-response-2026-08-05`) and 20.0% (`cr-v7-2026-08-18`), so v10 landing at chance is the result the rework was aiming for.

- **2026-09-05** — **THE "~450 BROKEN LIVE ITEMS" CONCLUSION IS A MODEL NUMBER, AND THE ONLY HUMAN DATA ON THE SAME TWO COHORTS DISAGREES WITH IT BY ~55 POINTS.** Yesterday I measured live Craft and Structure at **97.5%** blind and Information and Ideas at **91.9%**, over 54 and 86 items with 9-12 model solvers, and wrote that ~450 items are rewrite-scale. **B2 already sat those same two live cohorts with a human: Craft and Structure 8/20 = 40.0%, Information and Ideas 8/20 = 40.0%.**

      cohort                model solvers (2026-09-04)    human sitting (B2)
      Craft and Structure   97.5%  (n=54)                 40.0%  (n=20)
      Information & Ideas   91.9%  (n=86)                 40.0%  (n=20)

  **This is the ACT pattern exactly** — model 76-79% against the co-founder's 10.0% — and the register already holds seven TOEFL cohorts where the attack said 83-100% and a person scored 13-27%. The standing rule in CLAUDE.md is that the blind attack is a SCREEN and a human sitting is the VERDICT. I quoted that rule repeatedly yesterday and then built a rewrite plan on the screen anyway, because the model numbers were dramatic and internally consistent across two independent runs. Consistency between two model runs is not evidence about people.

  **What the human number actually says is neither "fine" nor "broken":** 40.0% sits inside the pre-registered 36-59% DEAD ZONE, and `B2-PREREGISTERED.md` closed the obvious escape in advance — *"if a cohort lands at 36%, it is inconclusive, not basically cleared."* So it does not clear them either. It says one reader was not enough, which is precisely what **B6** exists to resolve.

  **CONSEQUENCE, and it is the cheap direction:** do NOT start a 450-item rewrite. The next instrument is B6 — a second human reader — and it is ~20 minutes of Andy's time against a programme that would touch a third of the live R&W bank and, on yesterday's own evidence, risks introducing new tells in every item it touches. If B6 lands low, the model runs were an over-call and almost nothing needs rewriting. If B6 lands high, the rewrite is justified on human evidence rather than on a screen.

  **B6 is blocked on a calibration, and that calibration is already drawn and untouched:** `calibration-andy-2026-09-02`, 20 of 20 still unseen, on `andy@classraum.com` — the ONE open run on the whole bank. It must be Andy and not the co-founder, who holds every human sitting here; a second pass by him measures his own consistency, which is how B1 died. Skipping the calibration is what produced four consecutive unusable sittings before B4. _(the rewrite is PAUSED pending B6; the calibration is the unblocking step)_

- **2026-09-11** — **`legal == 1` IS NOT A PROXY FOR SOLVABILITY, AND THE SIXTH STRUCTURAL PROXY DIES HERE.** A 24-item matched live control on Information and Ideas (`ctrl-ii-c`, drawable only) was solved options-only by three independent solvers. All three returned the **identical** 24-character pick string `ADBCBBADCDBACABCCACBABAD` and scored **24/24 = 100.0%** — while reporting **`legal == 1` exactly ZERO times in 72 votes.** Not one item could be shown to have a single legal option; every item was answered correctly by everyone.

  The `mc_hidden_source` gate rule — *zero items with any confidently rejectable option* — was about to be relied on. It is necessary and nowhere near sufficient: a batch can score perfectly against it and still be fully solvable. The elimination check asks "can you prove the other three illegal?"; the leak answers "which one is the author's key?" All three solvers named the same mechanism unprompted — in 20 of 24 sets exactly one option is hedged or two-sided and the rest are absolutes (*entirely, proves, no role at all, every category, permanently*). No absolute is illegal. It is simply not how a careful author writes a key. **Score the attack; never gate on `legal`.** Sixth proxy to fail, same way as the other five (`OPTION-BALANCE-RESULT.md`): it measured a mechanism instead of the outcome.

  Two further live channels the solvers found, invisible to every checker in the repo: **numeric self-corroboration** (two options quote the same cell, pinning it, so any option contradicting it dies with the figure hidden — a consequence of building distractors by perturbing cells of a real table, found independently in `sat-ii-v1` by all three of its attackers); and **stem-option axis mismatch** on support/undermine stems.

  **These are MODEL numbers and they change no verdict about the live bank.** B2's human sitting on the same two cohorts scored 40.0% / 40.0% against 97.5% / 91.9% model, and today's 93.1% / 100.0% merely reproduce the model side. No rewrite programme; the unblocking step is still B6. Full write-up: `RW-LIVE-CONTROL-2026-09-11.md`.

- **2026-09-11** — **THE CANDIDATE R&W BATCHES ARE LESS LEAKY THAN THE LIVE BANK ON THE SAME INSTRUMENT, AND EXPRESSION OF IDEAS IS TWO STRATA.** Same-day, same-protocol comparison: Information and Ideas live 100.0% vs `sat-ii-v1` 69.4%; Craft and Structure live 93.1% vs `sat-cs-v5` 40.3%; Expression of Ideas live 45.8% vs `sat-eoi-v7` 37.5%. Both sides solved by the same solvers under the same protocol, so the comparison survives the model/human gap even though the absolute numbers do not.

  Stratifying EoI by its own STEM TEXT (`/transition/i`) splits the live cohort into **27.8% on 18 transition items and 100.0% on 6 rhetorical-synthesis items** (6/6 unanimous, 16 of 18 votes `legal == 1`). The 45.8% cohort mean is a blend in an 18:6 ratio that describes neither half — the table row above is corrected. The candidate splits the same way at 25.6% / 51.5%, so it is clean on transitions and half as leaky as the bank on synthesis. The synthesis mechanism is a **completeness test on the option text**: the stem enumerates what the answer must contain (two studies, both figures, the self-report AND the measurement) and distractors are built by DROPPING one part. Repair is on the distractor side; keys and letters cannot reach it.

  **Disposition: `sat-ii-v1` does NOT ship as authored** (69.4%, 16 of 24 unanimous, attackers agree on the mechanism). `sat-cs-v5` and `sat-eoi-v7` are held for a distractor-side pass on their leaky stratum, not a key rewrite.

- **2026-09-11** — **THE CONTROL SAMPLER WAS PAGING WITHOUT AN ORDER BY, AND WAS SAMPLING STAGED ITEMS INTO "LIVE" CONTROLS.** `attack-cohort.mjs` read both `study_item_bank` and `study_item_attacks_fresh` with `.range()` and no `.order()` — the trap CLAUDE.md records twice. An unordered paged read can repeat rows on one page and never return others, so the sampler could silently omit part of the population while marking the rest considered. Both reads now `.order()`.

  `--drawable` was added, restricting the sample to `verified=true`, because a control mixing in items the assembler never serves is not a measurement of the shipped bank. Break-tested against live counts rather than asserted: Craft and Structure 288 → 277 (11 staged excluded), Expression of Ideas and Information and Ideas unchanged at 244 and 250 — it does something where there is something to do and nothing where there is not.

  Also recorded because it nearly went the flattering way: the first EoI control seed dealt the key to **B on 13 of 24**. A letter-biased solver would have scored high on the CONTROL, inflating it, which makes any candidate look better by comparison. Re-seeded to 7/6/6/5. The sampler re-letters every item, so letters carry nothing and seeding for a flat deal costs no validity — but a control's deal has to be checked, because its errors all push in the direction nobody is watching.

- **2026-09-11** — **44 MATHS ITEMS INSERTED (ACT +20, ISEE +24), AND THE RUN THAT ALMOST BLOCKED THEM WAS MY OWN BAD INSTRUMENT.** Both batches cleared all four `mc_stem_source` stages. Sandbox 24/24 and 30/30, distractors 72/72 and 90/90, exhaustive break-tests (72 and 90 promotions, zero survivors) with the harnesses themselves attacked so the refusals count as evidence. Three with-source graders each: **every key agreed 3/3, every item exclusive, zero weak-distractor votes on either batch.**

  **The no-source stage had to be re-run because the first run was invalid.** I scored `act-math-v3-sp` at 68.1% pooled, 13 of 24 unanimous, and treated it as a fail. That number came from a prompt I wrote which handed the solvers the full stem **plus a written list of elimination heuristics to look for** — it measures the prompt. The repo's maths baseline (24-29%, `MATH-ATTACK-RESULT-2026-09-04.md`) comes from `make-options-only.mjs`, which **strips the stem entirely**. Different instruments; I compared them. Several "leaks" it surfaced were not tells at all — bounding a probability under 1/2 by symmetry, a combined rate lying between its two group rates — but ordinary quantitative reasoning the real ACT rewards. Re-run through the canonical render, keys dealt flat:

        act-math-v3-sp   27.8%  (25.0 / 33.3 / 25.0)   margin  +2.8   confident subset 1 of 21
        isee-math-s10    32.2%  (33.3 / 23.3 / 40.0)   margin  +7.2   confident subset 15 of 52

  ACT's confident subset is the sharpest single number here: solvers claimed confidence on 21 picks and were right on **one**. That is what a clean option set looks like from the inside.

  **10 items were still dropped, on unanimity rather than on the mean.** Four ACT and six ISEE items were solved by ALL THREE solvers, against a chance expectation of 0.38 and 0.47 items. A 7-point mean can hide a handful of fully decidable items, and the unanimity count finds them where the mean does not. All three ISEE solvers independently named the same mechanism for theirs, and it is specific and fixable: **a three-term arithmetic or geometric run plus one outlier names its own middle**, because distractors were built as key ± one step plus a blunder value. The clean shape they also agreed on: an EVEN-count run with no median, or a closed sign/reciprocal quartet. Fed forward to `isee-math-s11`.

  **Capacity: ISEE Math 283 → 307 (6 forms). ACT Math 229 → 249 and STILL 3 route-aware forms** — the batch was Statistics (32 → 56) while the binding domain is **Functions at 24 items**. Relieving a domain that was not the constraint moved the route-aware number by zero. Next ACT Math batch must be Functions. `verify-act-draw.ts` green on all four sections.

  **A grader finding recorded and deliberately NOT acted on:** in 13 of 24 ACT items the key was the single option breaking the other three's ascending run — decidable, worth ~59% blind, and invisible to `verify-answer-key-spread.ts`, which saw a flat 6/6/6/6. It is unreachable. `shuffleDrawnChoices` re-deals every `multiple_choice` item per session (all 1,752 maths rows are `multiple_choice`), and over 300 seeded draws of that exact shape the non-key options come back ascending 17.0% against the 16.7% a uniform shuffle of three gives. Repairing it would have been another rewrite of sound items. The same discovery did expose a real defect in the instrument, fixed separately: `renderBlind` was dealing maths options in AUTHORED order, so every maths attack ever run through it measured a permutation no student is served.

- **2026-09-11** — **AGREEMENT IS NOT THE SIGNAL; AGREEMENT x CORRECTNESS IS. THE SAME DAY PRODUCED BOTH POLES.** Two runs, hours apart, same three-solver options-only protocol:

        run                         agreement      score      reading
        LIVE Information & Ideas    byte-identical 100.0%     the option sets decide the item
        isee-verbal-s10 candidate   21-25 of 30     16.7%     the option sets MISLEAD, in unison

  On `isee-verbal-s10` all three solvers converge on the same picks and score **below chance** (16.7% against 25.0%), with a pooled confident subset of **6 of 40 = 15.0%**. They agreed, and they were agreeing on the wrong option. Every one of them named the same heuristic — *three options cluster on one axis and the odd one out is the key* — and the batch is built the other way round: the attractive singleton is a DISTRACTOR. A solver applying the standard option-set rule is actively punished. That is the strongest authoring result measured in this repo, and it is invisible to a rate read on its own, because 16.7% alone looks like noise around chance rather than a designed inversion.

  So high inter-solver agreement means the option sets are DETERMINATE, not that they are leaky. Which of the two it is comes from the score. Report both, always — this is the rule recorded earlier this week ("report inter-solver agreement alongside every attack rate") now given its second, opposite worked example.

- **2026-09-11** — **`ssat-verbal-s10` IS UNDECIDED AND THE POOLED MEAN HIDES WHY.** 28.9% against a 20.0% chance line (5-choice) looks like a +8.9 leak. It is one solver: **50.0 / 16.7 / 20.0**, inter-solver agreement 8, 12 and 18 of 30 against a ~6.0 chance floor, and the pooled **confident subset is 6 of 31 = 19.4%, dead on the 20.0% chance line.** Every structural rule the three solvers stated — relation-class singleton in the analogies, valence outlier under a shared affix, register break — produced picks no better than guessing. Solver a reached 15 of 30 with only **3** confident picks, i.e. from unstated intuition on items it had itself called coin flips.

  Disposition: 4 items solved by all three (chance expectation 0.24) are dropped; the rest go to a with-source grade, and the batch does not insert on this evidence alone. A pooled mean carried by one of three solvers is the shape CLAUDE.md already records ("solver spread is larger than the effect" — 2/5/20 rejections on one C&S render, three SSAT solvers agreeing on 8 of 30).

  Both verbal runs were scored through the width fixes committed the same day; before them, this SSAT run would have been compared to a 25.0% line it never faced and read as **margin +3.9 instead of +8.9**.

- **2026-09-11** — **"ELIMINATE THE LARGEST OPTION" IS WORTH 2.6 POINTS BANK-WIDE, AND THAT IS THE CEILING, NOT A DEFECT.** The `isee-math-s11` author reported, honestly and unprompted, that their key magnitude rank was 5/14/7/3 over 29 numeric items — the key is the largest option on only 3 — giving a blind solver who always drops the largest a **+4.9pt** edge. Measured against the population before treating it as theirs:

        LIVE MATHS BANK, key rank by magnitude among its own options
          4-choice  n=1,499   rank 1-4:  18.1%  33.1%  31.7%  17.1%   chance 25.0%
          5-choice  n=149     rank 1-5:  12.8%  26.2%  27.5%  23.5%  10.1%   chance 20.0%
          "always eliminate the largest" gains  +2.6pts (4-choice)  +2.5pts (5-choice)

  The whole bank already has this shape, in both widths, and the batch sits ~2.3 points above it on a sample of 29 — inside noise at that n. The cause is the one the author named: **wrong arithmetic paths overshoot far more often than they undershoot**, so the extremes are disproportionately distractors. That is inherent to building distractors from named error paths, which is the thing we most want authors to do. Flattening it would mean inventing distractors with no named path behind them — a strictly worse trade, and every touched item is a chance to introduce a new tell.

  On the TOEFL batch all three solvers agreed on **every item in every split file**, and the cue they named was near-unanimously recall, not option shape: ogives and Forbes bands, the gridiron pendulum, a tontine share dying with the subscriber, plinthite hardening irreversibly, ferric meaning oxidised meaning excess air. One solver said the bare `[Academic — Ceramics]` tag alone decided a vocabulary item. The author had deliberately chosen eight narrow, non-canonical fields — glaciology, horology, celadon kiln atmosphere, tontines, qanat gradient, S/Z twist, plinthite, Vitruvian echeia — against a live bank that repeats nine canonical topics. **Narrow subject choice is not enough against a model that knows all eight fields.**

  **The ACT Science route does not transfer.** `act-science-v6` and `v7` beat recall by INVENTING the subject — v7 never even names the suspended solid chemically, describing it only by relation. That is available because a science passage may describe a fictional experiment. **It is not available to a passage that must stay factually true**, which is every TOEFL, SAT and ACT Reading passage. So the two families split: invented-stimulus families can author recall away, prose-passage families cannot.

  Consequence, and it is a scheduling fact rather than an authoring one: on prose-passage families the model attack measures the model's world knowledge, and the only instrument that separates that from a student's is a human sitting. This is the register's seven TOEFL cohorts at 83-100% model against 13-27% human, now with a named mechanism.

The statistic that decides is therefore *among items with exactly one such pair, how often is the key in it*, against a 50% control (a uniformly random key sits in a given 2-of-4 pair half the time):

        items with exactly one such pair     173 of 1,664 scorable (10.4%)
        ...and the key is in that pair       125 = 72.3%   control 50.0%
        P(>= 125 | p = 0.5)                  2.1e-9

  A solver who finds the unique pair and guesses between its two members scores **36.1% against 25.0%** on those items, +11.1 points; bank-wide about +1.2. Small in aggregate, large on the items it touches, and those items are findable by name. The self-test fires on the motivating case, refuses a pair of two DISTRACTORS summing to 180 (which tells a solver nothing), refuses a near miss at 179, and includes a break-test showing the key-membership rule is what suppresses the distractor case rather than an accident.

- **2026-09-11** — **THE BLIND-RENDER GUARD REFUSED TWO SOUND ITEMS, AND THE TOOL HAD BEEN WRITING RENDERS UNDER THE WRONG NAME ALL ALONG.** Three defects in `make-grade-render.mjs`, all mine, all found by pointing it at four batches at once rather than one.

      AM4F-24   choices ["8","-2","2","24"]   refused on the field `id`
      IM11-08   choices ["1.5","0","2","1"]   refused on the field `prompt`

  Neither is a leak. The string `"AM4F-24"` *contains* `-2`, `2` and `24` as substrings, so an item's own label "named" three of its four options. `IM11-08` is a median question whose stem reads *"5 players scored 0 goals, 2 scored 1 goal, 3 scored 2 goals"* — listing its data is what that item type DOES, and it says nothing about which option is right.

  Both are one mistake: treating *"this text contains the option string"* as *"this text identifies the option as wrong."* The leak the guard was built for (`distractor_steps`) enumerates the WRONG options and makes the key the set complement. That is a property of **metadata, never of the stimulus** — and this is the with-source render, where the stimulus is shown on purpose. The guard now skips `prompt`/`passage`/`graphic` and strips the item's own id from every field before scanning. The exemption is an allow-list on the stimulus side only, so an unrecognised new field is still scanned: the direction that has to stay safe is unchanged.

  **The third defect was silent and older.** `const tag = args[args.indexOf('--out') + 1] ?? basename` — when `--out` is absent `indexOf` returns `-1`, so this read `args[0]`, the input **path**, as the tag. Every render made without `--out` was written to `scripts/study-bank/scripts/study-bank/<path>.grade.json`. It happened to crash here on the missing directory; had that directory existed it would have written a correct render under a name nobody would ever look for, and the grade would have been taken on a stale file. A sentinel index used as an array index is the whole bug.

  All three are in the self-test as regressions, with the two real items copied in verbatim rather than stylised, plus the marginal case that matters: **the same text moved into a metadata field must still refuse.** Without it, exempting the stimulus by skipping `prompt` wholesale would have passed silently. Each fix was reverted separately and fails exactly one assertion — a suite that only goes red when all three are gone would not have told me which mechanism mattered.

  One more, found by the self-test and invisible to the render path: `const STIMULUS` declared next to `optionLeak` sat in the temporal dead zone for `--selftest`, which runs earlier in the file. `ReferenceError` on the test path, fine on the real path, because by then the module is fully evaluated. Moved to the top with its siblings.

- **2026-09-11** — **MY BRIEF TOLD TWO READING AUTHORS THE WRONG FIELD NAME, AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT.** I instructed them to group items by `passage_group_id`. Nothing errors, nothing warns, and `bank-state` counts the rows as drawable — then the assembler drops every one of them, because `groupKeyOf` turns a null group id into `'__solo:' + id` and a singleton is not a passage.   **One of the two authors caught it and the other did not have to, because the first said so in their report.** They went to `verbal-bank-helper.mjs` before trusting the brief, found the mapping, used `topic_id`, and wrote: *"Had I written `passage_group_id`, every row would have landed null and been dropped as a singleton set."* That is the behaviour the brief asks for and it is worth naming: **when a brief and the code disagree, the code is what runs.**

  Neither `AUTHORING-BRIEF.md` nor `RUNBOOK.md` documented the field at all, which is how a wrong name survived being written into a commission. Now §6b of the brief, with the mapping quoted and the silent-failure path spelled out. The second reading batch is checked and corrected before it goes near an inserter.

  The general lesson is not about this field. **An instruction I wrote is not evidence about the code**, and a subagent following my brief exactly will reproduce my error at scale — eight at a time, in this session's case. - **2026-09-11** — **THE OPTIONS-ONLY ATTACK HAS A FLOOR ON VOCABULARY, AND COMPARING A VERBAL BATCH AGAINST A BARE 25.0% CONDEMNS SOUND ITEMS.**

  `isee-verbal-s12` measured 36.7% blind against a 25.0% chance line, +11.7, with 6 of 30 items solved by all three solvers. That reads as a leak, and it is not.

  What made me check: four of the six unanimously-solved items had solver `why` fields reading **"bare guess"** and **"no structural tell"**. Three solvers guessing independently do not converge on the right answer six times. They are not independent — same model, same prior over which of four words a test would key. On bare numerals that prior carries nothing, which is exactly why maths measures clean; on vocabulary it carries a great deal, and **it is partly the construct the item is trying to test.**

  So: 30 ALREADY-SHIPPED ISEE verbal items, drawn from five live cohorts, excluding the cohort under test, through the identical render.

        run                         n    mean    chance   margin   unanimous
        LIVE SHIPPED (control)     30   40.0%    25.0%    +15.0        7
        isee-verbal-s12            30   36.7%    25.0%    +11.7        6

  **The candidate scores BELOW the live bank.** The +11.7 is an instrument floor, not a property of the batch. Acting on it would have started a rewrite of a batch that is better than what students are already being served — the `measure the population before believing the backlog` failure, arriving through a new door.

  **Consequence, and it is not small: every verbal/prose margin this project has quoted against a 25.0% or 20.0% literal is suspect.** The numbers in the CLAUDE.md leaky/clean table (analogies 69.0%, words-in-context 12.5%/33.3%, and the rest) were computed that way. The clean ones stay clean — a floor only pushes up — but the leaky ones are overstated by an unknown amount, and the right comparator is a matched live control of the same section, same width, same render. **`ctl-isee-verbal.batch.json` is in the repo as the first one.**

  Maths is unaffected: the same argument predicts no floor there, and the four maths runs the same day came in at +2.4, +8.3, +11.7 and +13.3 with the leaks traced to exact, mechanically checkable shapes.

- **2026-09-11** — **SHARED OPTION POOLS: A FOURTH CHANNEL THAT DISSOLVED AGAINST THE POPULATION, AND THE SPLIT THAT DID IT.** `check-shared-pool.mjs` is in the repo, negative result and all.

  Two control solvers, independently, reading shipped ISEE verbal items with the stems withheld, reported the same two pairs of items sharing an identical option pool and called it an authoring artifact. It is decidable, so it was measured over the whole bank rather than the 30 items it was noticed in.

        multiple-choice rows                                5,615
        items sharing a pool with another item                295  (5.25%)
        ...of those, same key (near-duplicates)               143
        ...of those, DIFFERENT key (the exploitable shape)     152

  152 looked like a finding. **Two splits killed it.**

  First: **prose versus numeric.** A maths pool of `{4, 5, 6, 7}` collides with another item's constantly and by pure coincidence — short options from a tiny alphabet. Four prose definitions do not collide by accident. 152 splits into **77 prose** and **75 numeric**, and reporting the combined rate would have inflated a real defect roughly twofold with arithmetic coincidence. Same shape as the conditional-rate-versus-population-rate error already in this file.

  Second, and it finished the job: **72 of the 77 prose items sit in ONE `passage_group_id` each.** They are deliberate matching sets — five analogies sharing five options, each keyed to a different one — drawn and served together, which is a legitimate psychometric format and the thing `insert-verbal-sets.mjs` exists to enforce. Only **5 items** are ungrouped, and 3 of those are ACT Science trend questions where "increases steadily" recurs across unrelated figures.

  **Real cases: effectively zero.** The channel joins stem-echo, key-is-sum and key-magnitude on the dissolved list. It is worth recording precisely because two capable readers flagged it in good faith from a 30-item sample, and the population said no.

        ssat-reading-s11 (candidate)         30   66.7%    20.0%    +46.7       14

A solver's account of a channel is a hypothesis about where to look, never a measurement of what it yields — and on this pair of runs the identical account was correct about the mechanism in both cases and predictive in neither.
